newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Zinny contracted till end 1998 - NZRFU.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Zinny contracted till end 1998 - NZRFU.

text.p: WELLINGTON, June 11 - Whatever happens in contract talks between All Black Zinzan Brooke and his New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) employers, Brooke will play his rugby in New Zealand until the end of 1998, NZPA reported on Wednesday.
NZRFU chief executive David Moffett said he was "flabbergasted" by reports that Brooke was having trouble organising a new contract and that he might go overseas as a result.
"Zinny is contracted to us until the end of 1998," Moffett said.
"And we've been having very amicable discussions with him about his future."

The reports came from yesterday's Fiji-Counties match, where Counties coach Mac McCallion is reported to have suggested Brooke was having trouble reaching a contractual agreement and might be looking overseas.
A fortnight ago Brooke, amid rumours he might be considering a lucrative offer to play in Britain, said he expected to sign his contract on Tuesday last week.
The NZRFU is in the process of "rolling over" contracts with leading players at present.
Moffett says many contracts have been completed with the present All Black squad, with a few to go -- Brooke being one of them.
Brooke is likely to return to the All Blacks for next week's Wellington test match with Argentina.
Otago's Taine Randell will play in the No 8 position against Fiji on Saturday in Albany.
There were still about 7000 tickets to sell yesterday for the Albany match. The North Harbour stadium holds 25,000 people.
Sales for the Wellington test, against Argentina on June 21, reached 16,000 by early today.
